from: chapitre 4 de la vidéo longue (DeepSeek, paradoxe de Jevons)
hook: Cheaper AI was supposed to *sink Nvidia.*
paragraphs: On {January twenty-seventh, 2025,|January 27, 2025,} a Chinese lab called DeepSeek said it had trained a strong AI model for under {six million dollars.|$6 million.}
That day, Nvidia lost {five hundred and ninety-three billion dollars|$593 billion} of market value, the biggest one-day loss for any company on Wall Street.
The fear made sense on paper. Cheaper AI should need fewer chips.
But economists have a name for what often happens instead: the Jevons paradox. When something becomes cheaper to use, people find so many new uses for it that total demand goes up, not down.
In the quarter of the DeepSeek scare, Nvidia's revenue was about {thirty-nine billion dollars.|$39 billion.} Eighteen months later, it was {ninety-six.|$96 billion.}
Cheaper AI didn't shrink the market for Nvidia's chips. It helped put AI everywhere. Full story on the channel.
